synopsis: Gaussian splatting is used to rebuild scenes from recordings, with SplatAD and NVIDIA NuRec named as examples [f15954]. The ISPRS 2024 hybrid pipeline required invisible collision substrates beneath its Gaussian-splatting representation, indicating that this example needed additional geometry for collisions [f3914, f13129]. For sensor simulation, SplatAD (CVPR 2025) models rolling shutter, lidar intensity and ray dropout in real time, but the cited evidence is on-road rather than heavy off-road [f4516]. Whether neural or Gaussian-splatting reconstruction, including NuRec and related methods, can qualify as test evidence rather than training data remains uncertain [f9355].

relations.note: The glossary restates the collision-substrate requirement of the cited pipeline.
